PHP2Shell Exposure Accelerator

Runs in your own Azure subscription. It finds your PHP workloads, checks them against the PHP2Shell vulnerable-version table (CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619), and gives each owner a prioritised remediation plan. It uses four Azure AI Foundry agents, Azure Resource Graph and two small App Service apps.

Fixed releases
8.5.12 · 8.4.27 · 8.3.36 · 8.2.35
Deployment
One script: deploy.ps1
Footprint
B1 plan + Foundry project
Run cost
B1 plan + typically cents of model tokens per assessment
Get the code on GitHubgithub.com/dustyFski/php2shell-exposure-accelerator Open repository →
🛡️

Defensive and read-only. The accelerator reads response headers and Azure resource metadata, compares versions and advises. It does not change workloads, install patches or send exploit payloads. Workload owners still apply the patches, guided by the remediation plan.

01

Before you start

Whoever runs deploy.ps1 needs the following tools and permissions.

Tools

  • PowerShell 7+ (Windows, macOS or Linux)
  • Azure CLI 2.60+ with Bicep
  • Python 3.10+
  • Model quota for the chosen model in -FoundryLocation (default gpt-4.1-mini, GlobalStandard)

Permissions

  • Owner (or Contributor + User Access Administrator) on the target resource group, because the template creates role assignments
  • If the resource group doesn't exist yet: permission to create it in the deployment subscription. The script also registers the Microsoft.Web and Microsoft.CognitiveServices resource providers there, which needs subscription-level rights unless they are already registered
  • Permission to create Entra ID app registrations and assign users to enterprise applications (Application Administrator or Cloud Application Administrator, or ownership of the portal app)
  • Reader-granting rights (User Access Administrator or Owner) on every subscription in -InventorySubscriptionIds
02

Deploy

Sign in with az login, then clone the repository and run the script from its root folder. It is safe to run again on the same resource group.

git clone https://github.com/dustyFski/php2shell-exposure-accelerator.git
cd php2shell-exposure-accelerator
./deploy.ps1 -SubscriptionId <sub-id> -ResourceGroup rg-php2shell -Location swedencentral `
             -InventorySubscriptionIds <sub-a>,<sub-b>

What the script does

  1. 1
    Check prerequisites

    Azure CLI, Python and SDKs; registers resource providers.

  2. 2
    Create resource group

    In the region given by -Location.

  3. 3
    Entra app registrations

    Portal sign-in (single tenant, assigned users only) and the checker API audience api://….

  4. 4
    Bicep deployment

    App Service plan, two web apps, Easy Auth, Foundry account / project / model (or reuse an existing one), RBAC.

  5. 5
    Grant Reader

    To the checker API identity, on each subscription in -InventorySubscriptionIds.

  6. 6
    Deploy app code

    Zip-deploy; Oryx builds on App Service. Checks the real deployment result.

  7. 7
    Create agents

    create_agents.py creates 4 prompt agents with managed-identity OpenAPI tools; re-runs add a version only if an agent changed.

  8. 8
    Finish

    Revokes the temporary deployer role, prints the portal URL and agent names, and writes cleanup-<resource-group>-<sub-id-prefix>.ps1.

ℹ️

Who can sign in. Only you at first. Add colleagues with -PortalUserObjectIds / -PortalGroupObjectIds or under Enterprise applications → the portal app → Users and groups.

First sign-in. Each user sees a one-time Entra consent prompt for basic profile access to the portal app. An Entra admin can approve it for the whole organisation instead: Enterprise applications → the portal app → Permissions → Grant admin consent.

03

Use the portal

Open the portal URL printed by the script and sign in with your organisation account. The left panel sets what to check; the three tabs on the right give you three ways to run the check.

1 · Tell it what to check

Enter websites or hostnames (one per line) and, optionally, an Azure subscription ID to inventory. The first ID in -InventorySubscriptionIds is pre-filled (by default, the deployment subscription): clear it for a URLs-only check, because leaving it set inventories that subscription and header-checks up to 200 of its app hostnames.

2 · Add context

Pick Hosting (for example App Service Linux) and Edge / WAF. The advisor tailors fixes and mitigations to them.

3 · Confirm ownership

Tick “I confirm my organisation owns these systems or is authorised to assess them.” The instant scan and the multi-agent assessment won't run without it.

Multi-agent assessment

Uses AITypically under a minute
  1. Click ▶ Run multi-agent assessment.
  2. The URL Scanner and Azure Inventory agents run in parallel. Each card shows its timing and the API operations it called.
  3. The Remediation Advisor then turns both sets of findings into a prioritised plan.
  4. Scroll down for each agent's table and the final plan.

Use it for the full, explained assessment you hand to workload owners.

Instant scan

No AISeconds
  1. Click ⚡ Instant scan (no AI).
  2. The portal calls the checker API directly: the header check for every URL plus the Azure inventory of the subscription.
  3. Summary tiles count the URL checks (checked, vulnerable, unknown, OK); the Azure inventory appears separately below.
  4. The inventory table shows each app's configured PHP stack, advertised version and who patches: the platform or you. If the advertised version differs from the configured stack, it is flagged with ⚠ instead, because the configured stack then says nothing reliable about what serves traffic.

Use it for a quick triage, or to re-check after patching.

Ask the agent

Uses AIConversational
  1. Type a question, or start from a suggestion:
Check my sitesPHP 8.1 on VMsInventory my AzureCheck a version
  1. The Orchestrator agent decides which checker operations to call and answers with fixes, Azure-specific guidance, detection steps and sources.
  2. Follow-up questions keep the conversation context.

Use it for “what if” questions, servers outside Azure (paste php -v output), and explaining results.

04

Read the results

Every system gets one of three statuses. End-of-life branches (8.1 and older) are also flagged in every result: even with PHP's minimal backports for 7.4, 8.0 and 8.1, the advice is to migrate to a supported branch.

VULNERABLE

At or below the last vulnerable patch level

The advertised version is at or below the last vulnerable release of its branch.

P1 · Patch or upgrade now; add a WAF rule as an interim layer
UNKNOWN

Version hidden or unrecognised

Headers, a CDN or a proxy hide the version, or it isn't a recognised release. Hidden is not patched.

P2 · Confirm on the server
OK

Above the last vulnerable patch level

The advertised version is a fixed release. Headers are evidence, not proof.

P3 · Verify on the server (php -v for the SAPI in use)

Who patches on Azure

WorkloadWho applies the fix
App Service (Linux), built-in PHP 8.2+ stacksThe platform rolls out patched runtimes. Verify the running version.
Advertised version differs from the configured stack (flagged ⚠)Unknown until you verify the runtime that actually serves traffic (custom startup, container, proxy). Don't rule out end-of-life exposure or assume platform patching.
Container apps (DOCKER stacks)Listed as candidates; they may not run PHP. If they do, you rebuild on a patched base image.
End-of-life stacks, App Service on Windows with custom PHP, containers, VMs, AKSYou patch or upgrade.
Interim WAF layerFront Door WAF managed rule 99006001 (group MS-ThreatIntel-Response-CVEs, DRS 2.0–2.2): disabled by default, works only with Block on anomaly, rollout completes around 28 Oct 2026; contact Microsoft Support about expedited availability. Or an Application Gateway WAF v2 Set-Cookie rewrite rule. Both supplement patching; they don't replace it.
05

Architecture

New Azure compute and Foundry resources are deployed into one resource group; Entra app registrations and subscription-scoped role assignments are outside it, and a reused Foundry project can live elsewhere. Classifications come from the version table in the checker API code, so they are deterministic and auditable. The agent prompts also contain fixed-version and WAF guidance, which you must keep current along with the table.

ComponentAzure resourcePurpose
PortalMicrosoft.Web/sites (Python 3.12)Sign-in UI. Runs instant scans and calls the agents.
Checker APIMicrosoft.Web/sites (Python 3.12)Deterministic logic: header checks, version table, Resource Graph inventory, remediation rules. Exposed as an OpenAPI tool.
Foundry account + projectMicrosoft.CognitiveServices/accounts (AIServices) + /projectsHosts the four prompt agents and the model deployment. Local (key) auth is disabled.
Model deployment/accounts/deploymentsDefault gpt-4.1-mini (GlobalStandard, 50K TPM). Any chat model in the project works.
App Service planMicrosoft.Web/serverfarms (Linux B1)Shared by both apps.
Entra app registrations (2)Entra IDPortal sign-in (single tenant), and the api://… audience that protects the checker API.

Agent design

  • Each agent is a Foundry prompt agent with one OpenAPI tool. The tool spec is filtered to that agent's operations (least privilege at the tool level).
  • The Orchestrator powers Ask the agent and can call all six operations.
  • Multi-agent assessment runs the URL scanner and Azure inventory agents in parallel, then hands their findings to the Remediation advisor.
  • Shared guardrails on every agent: defensive only, no exploit content, unknown ≠ patched, headers are evidence not proof, cite php.net and the Azure Network Security blog.

Request flow

06

Identity & security

No keys or secrets: every service-to-service call uses a managed identity.

  • Checker API is not anonymous. App Service Authentication returns 401 unless the token audience is api://<checker client id> and the caller is an allow-listed managed identity. Only /healthz, /openapi.json and /docs are public, and they expose no scan or inventory data.
  • Least privilege. Reader only, only on the subscriptions you list. Each agent's tool spec contains only its operations.
  • Server-side scope. The checker API refuses inventory requests for any subscription you did not list, whoever asks, including the agents; the portal also checks instant scans.
  • Assigned users only. Sign-in is mandatory and limited to the users and groups assigned to the portal app. Anyone assigned can see the inventory of the listed subscriptions.
  • Public destinations only. URL checks refuse loopback, private, link-local and metadata addresses (also via DNS re-binding) and ports other than 80, 443, 8080 and 8443.
  • Bounded work. Only headers are read, never bodies; probes run at most 10 at a time per worker process (two workers by default); incomplete inventories are flagged.
  • Untrusted tool output. Header values are sanitised, and agents are instructed to treat headers and resource names as data, never as instructions. Instructions reduce prompt-injection risk; they don't guarantee it.
  • Foundry. A new Foundry account is created with disableLocalAuth: true, so no API keys. If you reuse a project, check the existing account's authentication settings.
  • HTTPS only, TLS 1.2 minimum, FTPS disabled.
  • Ownership confirmation before an instant scan or multi-agent assessment runs. It is an attestation, not a technical control, and Ask the agent has no checkbox; instant scans are logged with the signed-in user.
  • Data handling. The instant scan uses no AI. The AI features send scan targets and findings to your Foundry agents and model deployment; a GlobalStandard deployment may process them in any Azure region.
  • Safe probing. A HEAD request (GET only on 405/501) with a clearly labelled user agent (PHP2Shell-Checker-Azure/1.0 (defensive version check)); headers only. URL credentials and fragments are rejected.

07

Operate & clean up

Cost

One Linux B1 App Service plan, billed separately, plus model tokens per assessment (an estimate: typically a few cents per run with gpt-4.1-mini, depending on the number of systems). Instant scans use no model tokens.

Limits to keep in mind

  • Header checks are evidence, not proof: headers can be removed or changed, and Linux distributions backport fixes without changing the version string.
  • Inventory covers App Service through Resource Graph: configured PHP stacks plus container apps as candidates (verify what they run). Check VMs, AKS and on-premises servers by URL, or paste php -v output into Ask the agent.
  • Not an official Microsoft or PHP advisory. php.net and the Azure Network Security blog are the authoritative sources.

Remove everything

The deployment writes a clean-up script next to deploy.ps1, named with the first eight characters of the subscription ID. If the script created the resource group, clean-up deletes the entire group, including anything added to it later. In an existing group it removes only the resources the deployment recorded. It also removes the app registrations, role assignments and, in an existing Foundry project, the agents the deployment created, and it refuses to run against a different tenant. Check its output for warnings about anything left to remove by hand.

./cleanup-<resource-group>-<first-8-characters-of-subscription-id>.ps1
